source_snapshot.procedure: Open BMC Web Operations OEM Firmware, select each device for firmware update, then check the new versions.
source_snapshot.criteria: All device updates succeed and all new versions are correct.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL: stages files under /srv/fw, reads FirmwareInventory and defers flashing until approval.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION at CRITICAL risk; requires a complete OEM-device/image matrix, signature and compatibility proof, dependency order, per-device approval, task/activation monitoring and recovery.

historical_reviews.deepseek: Correctly avoids an unapproved flash, but its inventory query and staging do not identify every OEM device, validate images, execute updates or prove active versions.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly changes the incomplete workflow into a governed multi-device update and rejects bulk execution without per-device assurance.
historical_reviews.history: No earlier exact source identity record exists.
historical_reviews.v3_1: The phrase each device is a coverage matrix, not permission for a bulk transaction. Each device needs an independently auditable and recoverable update ledger, and any failed or ambiguous device stops later writes.

original_test_intent: Validate the BMC OEM Firmware workflow by updating every in-scope OEM device with its approved compatible image and proving the correct active version for each device.
original_method: Build the authoritative installed OEM-device matrix, bind each device to its owner-approved target version and signed compatible image, define dependency and activation order, preserve configuration and independent recovery, then update exactly one device per approved transaction with task/reboot monitoring and post-update active-version plus platform-health checks before proceeding to the next device.
manual_activity: The owner approves the complete device/version/image/order matrix and each irreversible activation; an operator maintains stable power and recovery access, observes every activation boundary and owns recovery and verdict decisions.
required_inputs: Complete installed OEM device and active/staged version matrix
Owner-approved target version for every in-scope device
Per-device authenticated image, checksum and signature
Stable power, maintenance window and bounded timeout
safety_requirements: Never interpret Select each device as authorization for bulk flashing
Bind every image to one exact hardware identity and activation slot
Validate signature, checksum, compatibility and dependency order before each upload
Use validated TLS and protected secret injection
Maintain stable power and recovery independent of the device being changed
Obtain final approval immediately before every activation
Do not proceed to another device after failure, ambiguity, access loss or health alarm
Do not automatically retry a failed or stalled task
Preserve update, audit, SEL and OS evidence without clearing logs
agent_execution_scope: Collect complete device, firmware, configuration and health baseline
Validate each image and proposed update order
Upload and activate one approved device only after confirmation
Monitor the one-device task, activation and reboot with bounded polling
Compare active version and platform health before requesting permission for the next device
Assist only owner-approved recovery and report evidence without assigning verdict
engineer_actions: Approve the complete OEM coverage matrix and exclusions
Approve image compatibility, dependency order and maintenance plan
Provide independent recovery and rollback for each device
Stop or authorize continuation after reviewing each result

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: FirmwareInventory is useful discovery evidence and /srv/fw may stage approved files, but neither proves image provenance, exact target binding, dependency order, update completion or active versions; TLS bypass and embedded credentials are unsafe.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the vendor-supported protected update path for one matrix entry at a time; record the device/image/task/activation tuple and prove the expected active version and health before any next write.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The all-device scope, new-version acceptance and 60/60-minute estimates remain; the actual device/image/version set is an owner input rather than inferred.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Maintain a per-device ledger containing stable hardware identity, baseline active/staged version, target image provenance/hash/signature, compatibility and order approval, task and activation events, post active version, health delta and recovery disposition.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes the source's broad all-device selection serial, gated and recoverable without removing any in-scope device.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Inventory discovery covers no writes; one successful firmware result cannot stand in for the remaining device matrix.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: OEM components can have coupled dependencies and different activation boundaries. Bulk selection can destroy fault isolation and make a partially updated platform unrecoverable.

project_override_considerations: The Project must enumerate what OEM Firmware means on this platform and distinguish it from row 1605's general single-component Firmware case. Shared images or dependencies do not permit combining devices into one unreviewed transaction.
expected_evidence: Approved complete OEM device/current-target-version/image/order matrix and explicit exclusions
Per-device hardware identity, signed image provenance, checksum/signature, compatibility, backup and recovery proof
Per-device final approval plus protected upload, task, activation and bounded reboot timeline
Per-device post-update inventory proving the intended active version on the same hardware identity
Platform configuration/health and update/audit/SEL/OS comparison after every transaction
Stop/recovery disposition for any failed or ambiguous entry and engineer-owned final verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source consistently requests updating all OEM devices and checking all new versions. The unspecified device population and images are required project inputs, not contradictory targets.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The device matrix, signed images, ordering and recovery package are normal vendor/project prerequisites that can be requested without guessing; execution remains gated until supplied.

review_improvement: Converts an unsafe bulk-selection concept into complete but sequential all-device coverage with per-device identity, approval, fault isolation and recovery.
independent_technical_reasoning: A multi-device firmware result is the conjunction of independently proven device results. Inventory names are not sufficient identities, and a version may be staged rather than active. Serial transactions preserve causal attribution: each task and health delta belongs to one device, and the first abnormal result prevents compounding damage on later devices.
